pf.license.need: Always. Each agent: their own state insurance license for the customer's state, with the line for that kind of insurance (health for Medicare and health plans, life for life insurance, property and casualty for home and auto). The agency: its own agency license where the state's rules require it.
pf.license.ask: Each agent's license number and lines, and the states they're licensed in, at sign-up or in their invite reply. The agency's license number. For Medicare plans: each agent's plan appointments and this year's plan training, from the agent's own records.
pf.license.how it's checked: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks going live: No agent licensed for a line in a customer's state: nothing of that kind is booked there. An agent whose plan training for the year isn't on file isn't offered for Medicare plans (a switch).
pf.license.renewals: optional reminders the owner sets; a license the owner says has lapsed pauses that person's new bookings for that work (the owner's word, never a check)
pf.license.unlicensed staff: An assistant with no insurance license, like Pat, books, moves, cancels and reminds only. They never talk about plans, coverage, plan prices or benefits.
pf.license.insurance: Errors-and-omissions insurance where the state's rules or the plan companies require it (a switch, from the state's form).
pf.license.background check: Part of the license itself, on the state's records. Rosie adds none.

pf.visit.check-in: Phone or video: the agent asks for the 4-digit code at the start, which also shows they're talking to the person who booked. At the office: the code at the front desk. At a home: the code at the door.
pf.visit.at check-in: The agent says their name, agency and license number, and that the meeting is free. For Medicare: they confirm the products on the signed scope form, and read the plan rules' statement (a switch).
pf.visit.recording: Phone meetings about Medicare plans are recorded in the agency's own tools where the plan rules require it (a switch). The agent says so at the start.
pf.visit.work changes: A product not on the scope form: a new scope form is signed first, before a word about it. Other insurance, like life insurance, waits for its own meeting where the plan rules say so (a switch). Extra time is free, with the customer's yes. A second meeting is its own booking.
pf.visit.the customer lives in another state: The agent stops talking about plans. Rosie offers an agent licensed there, if the agency has one, or says plainly it can't help there.
pf.visit.after the meeting: The customer decides in their own time. Any enrollment, application or policy change is done by the agent in the plan company's own app or the agency's own tools. The plan company sends its own confirmation.
pf.visit.home meetings: Only at the booked time. The agent never drops by (a switch, from the plan rules).
pf.visit.Rosie never: Quotes, compares, recommends, sells, binds or changes a policy, enrolls anyone, files a claim, or touches the agency's own tools.

pf.money.before: Nothing taken, and no card saved.
pf.money.after: Nothing to pay through Rosie. The insurance company pays the agent; premiums go to the insurance company, never through Rosie.
pf.money.fee-based review: Off by default. Only where the agency truly charges one and the state's rules allow an agent's fee (a switch from the state's form), with the customer's written fee agreement. Then it's billed the agency's own way, outside Rosie.
pf.money.fees: No cancel, late or no-show fee, ever.
pf.money.never: No deposit, hold, full price, premium or bill through Rosie.
pf.money.rosfield: The agency pays Rosfield's $2 per confirmed booking by default, never more than $49 a month per person, on the monthly bill (nothing is paid through Rosie). Rosfield's lawyer confirms before launch.

pf.messages.license numbers: Each text that names an agent shows their license number where the state's rules require it.
pf.messages.documents: A Medicare card, ID or policy photo texted by mistake is deleted, never passed on, and the customer is asked not to send them.
pf.messages.plan questions: Go to the agent on the secure page, with any numbers taken out. The agent answers at the meeting.
pf.messages.no nudges: Only replies and the reminders the customer agreed to. No plan offers, promotions, rating requests or 'book again' texts, and no 'review your plan next year' text unless the customer asks for one. Rosie never calls or texts anyone who didn't ask.
pf.messages.required statement: A switch, on by default: the plan rules' statement about how many plans the agency offers, on the secure page, in the first text and at the meeting's start. Its words and numbers come from the agency.
pf.messages.records: A switch, on by default: texts and scope forms kept as long as the plan rules require.
pf.messages.client notes: The agent's notes go in the agency's own tools. Rosie keeps only the time, the kind of meeting, the scope form and the outcome.

pf.staff.licenses: Each agent: their own license, lines and states. Rosie shows it as given and doesn't check it. Plan appointments and yearly plan training from the agent's own record (a switch).
pf.staff.skills: Medicare plans, life insurance, home and auto, seminars, Spanish.
pf.staff.supervision: An unlicensed assistant, like Pat, books, moves, cancels and reminds only, and never talks about plans or coverage.
pf.staff.who OKs: Sam OKs office and home meetings. Sam may let each agent OK their own.
pf.staff.fairness: Agents are offered by soonest time, never ranked by plan company, pay from a plan, or anything about the customer. Nobody is steered to or from an agent.

pf.rules.books right away: Phone and video meetings, and home meetings with a returning customer. Office meetings, same-day meetings and a new customer's home meeting ask Sam first (a switch).
pf.rules.the customer's state: Only agents licensed for that kind of insurance in the customer's state are offered (a switch, on: by the business's word on each license).
pf.rules.scope form: A switch, on by default: the scope form signed before any meeting about Medicare health or drug plans, where the plan rules require it.
pf.rules.required statement: A switch, on by default: the plan rules' statement about how many plans the agency offers.
pf.rules.recording: A switch: phone meetings about Medicare plans recorded in the agency's own tools where the plan rules require it.
pf.rules.home meetings: Only at a booked time, never a drop-in (a switch, from the plan rules).
pf.rules.plan season: Extra hours in the yearly enrollment season (the agency's setting). Its dates come from the plan rules (a switch).
pf.rules.named: The customer may name an agent. A named agent is never swapped on silence: Sam calls instead.
pf.rules.no cold contact: Rosie never calls or texts anyone who didn't ask: only replies and reminders the customer agreed to.
pf.rules.ratings: Off: no rating request after an insurance meeting (a switch, off by default).
pf.rules.listing words: A switch: words about Medicare plans follow the plan rules, and the agency OKs them before going live.
pf.rules.rosfield's $2: On by default; a switch for the rules on referral or lead fees in insurance (Rosfield's lawyer list).
pf.rules.referral pay: Rosfield takes nothing per policy, per enrollment or from an agent's pay, and never ranks agents.
pf.rules.license numbers in texts: On, where the state's rules require it (a switch from the state's form).
pf.rules.sharing: The customer's details never go to another agency or marketer without the customer's own written yes.
pf.rules.records: Rosie keeps times, the kind of meeting, scope forms and outcomes, plus the texts, as long as the plan rules require (a switch).
pf.rules.other insurance at a Medicare meeting: None is offered, like life insurance, where the plan rules forbid it (a switch). The customer books a separate meeting for it.
pf.rules.scope form on a call: A switch, off by default: where the plan rules allow it, the agency may take the scope form on a recorded call in its own tools instead of the secure page. Rosie then only notes that it's done.
pf.rules.stand-in scope form: A switch, from the plan rules: where the signed form names one agent, a stand-in gets a new one signed first, before any plan talk.

pf.edges.health or policy details in a request: Removed before anything is saved. The AI is told once.
pf.edges.a plan question: Passed to the agent privately, with numbers taken out. Rosie never advises.
pf.edges.a scam caller or a push to switch today: The scam warning first: 1-800-MEDICARE, the Elder Fraud Hotline for people 60 and older, and ReportFraud.ftc.gov for anyone. Then the booking goes on.
pf.edges.a family member pressing the customer: The agent talks with the customer alone first. No family details in Sam's text.
pf.edges.nobody licensed for that state or line: Nothing booked. Rosie says so plainly.
pf.edges.the scope form isn't signed: One reminder. Still not signed: Sam decides: keep it (signed at the start, before any plan talk), move it, or cancel with no fee.
pf.edges.a product not on the scope form: A new scope form is signed first.
pf.edges.the agent can't come: Sam offers another licensed agent, or calls. Nobody is moved on silence.
pf.edges.the customer wants to enroll: The agent does it in the plan company's own app, never Rosie.
pf.edges.a grown child books for a parent: The parent signs their own scope form and takes part.
pf.edges.the customer is in another state that da: The agent must also be licensed there where the state's rules require it (a switch).
